title: Finance Assistant
description:
Finance Assistant

Location: Norwich (West)

Salary: £30,000 - £35,000 depending on experience

Full-Time Permanent and office based (free parking)

Looking to Build a Long-Term Career in Finance?

Reed Accountancy, Norwich is working with a well-known business on the outskirts of Norwich who are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Finance Assistant to join their growing Finance team. Working closely with the Finance Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring accurate financial reporting, intercompany recharging, reconciliations, and analysis across multiple group businesses.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop their accounting experience within a supportive environment, with a clear pathway towards management reporting and broader finance responsibilities.

The Role

Initially, your focus will be on supporting the Finance Manager with the accurate allocation and recharging of costs across the group. As your knowledge and experience grow, you will take ownership of reporting activities and become involved in management accounts, forecasting, audit support, and wider financial analysis.

Key Responsibilities
- Calculate and process intercompany recharges by analysing financial data and liaising with Finance Managers across the group.
- Prepare journals and raise sales invoices to ensure accurate allocation of costs.
- Perform monthly bank reconciliations.
- Complete regular balance sheet reconciliations to ensure accuracy and integrity of financial records.
- Provide ad hoc financial analysis and reporting to management.

Future Development Opportunities

As your role develops, you will gain exposure to:
- Producing and reviewing trial balances at month-end.
- Updating monthly rolling forecasts for management review and group consolidation.
- Assisting in the preparation of half-year and year-end management accounts.
- Supporting the Tax team with required financial information.
- Supporting Internal Audit reviews.
- Assisting External Auditors during year-end audit processes.
- Contributing to financial reporting and business performance analysis.

About You

We are looking for someone who is:
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail.
- Comfortable working with financial data and large volumes of information.
- Analytical and confident using spreadsheets.
- A strong communicator who can build effective working relationships across departments.
- Proactive, eager to learn, and keen to develop their finance career.
- Able to manage deadlines and prioritise workloads effectively.

Skills & Experience
- Previous experience within a finance, accounts, or accounting support role.
- Good understanding of reconciliations, journals, and accounting principles.
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills.
- Experience using accounting systems would be advantageous
- Competent user of Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.

What's on Offer?
- Career progression and professional development opportunities.
- Exposure to management accounting and group finance activities.
- A varied role with increasing responsibility.
- Supportive and collaborative finance team.
- Competitive salary and benefits package.

If you're looking for an opportunity where you can develop beyond a traditional accounts support role and build a successful career in finance, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to take the next step in your finance career and call the Reed Norwich office to find out more information.

description:

- Client Care: Take instructions, explain legal terms, and provide estimates of fees.

title: HR Administrator
description:
HR Administrator

Location: Wymondham College, Wymondham

Salary: £26,403 - £28,142 per annum

Vacancy Type: Permanent, Full Time (37.5 hours per week)

At Sapientia Education Trust, our students are at the heart of everything we do, and our HR team plays a vital role in supporting the staff who make a difference every day. We are seeking an organised, proactive and professional individual to join our busy HR team as an HR Administrator. This is an exciting opportunity to support a wide range of HR activities across our growing Trust.

THE ROLE

the HR Administrator will provide comprehensive administrative support across the HR function, helping to coordinate recruitment activity, support employee relations processes and contribute to the effective delivery of HR services across the Trust.

The role includes the following:
- Coordinating recruitment activity, including arranging interviews and preparing recruitment documentation.
- Supporting onboarding processes and ensuring all pre-employment checks are completed.
- Preparing induction paperwork and coordinating mandatory training records.
- Providing administrative support to HR Managers and the wider HR team
- Coordinating investigations, formal meetings and casework processes
- Preparing correspondence, including meeting invitations and outcome letters.
- Taking accurate meeting notes and minutes.
- Producing reports and workforce data analysis as required
- Maintaining confidential HR records and documentation

PERSON SPECIFICATION

The personal competencies expected of an HR Administrator are:
- The ability to communicate clearly and tactfully using appropriate methods, high attention to detail and an awareness of the impact of your own communication on others;
- Able to maintain positive relationships with all and able to work as an effective and flexible part of a team; willing to change methods of work and routines to benefit the team;
- Willingness to accept responsibility for your own actions; the ability to prioritise effectively, meet deadlines and accept challenges.
- Ability to accept responsibility for own actions, prioritise workloads effectively, meet deadlines and respond positively to challenges.

The professional competencies expected of an HR Administrator are:
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills;
- Be flexible in managing and planning daily, weekly, monthly workloads;
- Have very good time management, planning and organisational skills;
- Able to work with minimum supervision and as part of a team;
- Be able to contribute to the analysis of problems and make suggestions for solutions;
- Have the ability to maintain confidentiality at all times, and use tact, diplomacy and empathy where necessary;
- Committed to providing the best possible service to the staff, governors, students and parents.

The qualifications and previous experience required of the HR Administrator are:
- A minimum of a grade C / 4, or equivalent, in English and Maths GCSE.
- Have a sound track record of good quality administration and be proficient in ICT database and software systems, particularly Microsoft Office, Access, Excel and Word;
- Experience of an HR or education environment would be beneficial, but not a requirement;
- Previous experience of the MHR iTrent MIS would be an advantage, but full training will be provided.

ABOUT US

The Sapientia Education Trust (SET) was established in 2016 with the purpose of bringing like-minded schools together to work in partnership to deliver a world class education to pupils in Norfolk and Suffolk. SET currently consists of 9 secondary schools and 14 primary schools, educating over 5,500 pupils.

WHAT WE OFFER
- A personal Sodexo account with access to high street discounts
- Flexibility on hours during the school holidays
- Assistance Wellbeing Support 24/7

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Sapientia Education Trust, please click apply to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

title: Emergency Call Handler - Ambulance
description:
Can you keep a cool head at times of crisis? Do you care about others? Do you want a career helping those in need? If the answer is yes, then this could be the job for you!

Please only apply if you can attend assessment on 6th October 2026 and can commence on 9th November 2026 and have no holiday planned for the first 5 weeks from 9th November.

We are looking for Call Handlers to work 12 hour shifts flexibly from Monday to Sunday. This will be a mixture of day and night shifts 7am-7pm and 7pm-7am. This role is initially on a temporary basis with a view to go permanent after about 6 months.

Training will take place from Monday to Friday, 8am to 4pm and within this time you must have no annual leave in the first 4 weeks of training.

Initial Pay Rates (uplift from week 13)
- £12.71 days (£13.58 from week 13)
- £17.16 Nights and Saturdays (£18.33 from week 13)
- £21.48 Sundays and Bank Holidays (22.95 from week 13)
- Saturdays (midnight to midnight) and Weekdays after 8 pm and before 6 am: Time plus 35%
- Sundays and Public Holidays (midnight to midnight): Time plus 69%

Our Emergency Call Handlers are committed, enthusiastic individuals who care about people. They must have the ability to listen and respond, processing information quickly and accurately into the Computer Aided Dispatch system. Customer service skills are important and the ability to remain calm and supportive as some callers will be experiencing significant distress and trauma, including the loss of a loved one. Being able to remain focused on giving the right advice and support despite experiencing the emotions of others is a real skill and strong calm communication is required.

All of the instructions and advice you will be giving to callers/patients is managed through a triage tool, it is intuitive and will present to you at the right time.

No clinical experience is required, and although some call-centre experience would be an advantage, it is not essential.

Main duties of the job

Answer 999 calls that come into the Emergency Operating Centre in a timely manner. Utilise the clinical triage software system you will have been trained in to deliver a category of response to our callers. Please note, there may be a change to this software, in the future and if so, full training will be provided. You are required to be polite, courteous and respectful at all times when talking to patients, callers and your peers, in line with the Trusts values and behaviours. Working for our organisation

Our Call Centre teams are a dedicated and resilient group, as the first point of contact with patients in their time of need.

Person specification

Qualifications

Essential criteria
- 4 GCSEs at grade C or above (or an equivalent qualification) including English or equivalent suitable Call Centre experience.

Skills & Knowledge

Essential criteria
- Effective verbal and written communication skills
- Work on own initiative
- Prioritise and undertake numerous tasks simultaneously
- Remain calm under pressure
- Work as part of a high performance team

Personal Attributes

Essential criteria
- High standards of personal professionalism
- Determination to meet targets
- Ability to judge priorities when dealing with emergency situations
- Willingness to learn
- Empathy and compassion

For more information about the client or the role please do call the Norwich office of Reed on and ask for Maxine, Isobelle or Andrea.

title: Patient Services Administrator
description: Due to internal progression, we have two fantastic opportunities to join our Patient Services Team. As part of Patient Services, you will play an important role in creating a positive experience for our patients. You will help people access the most appropriate support for their needs, whether that's within the practice or through services available across the wider NHS. Were looking for enthusiastic, adaptable people who can communicate confidently, think on their feet and stay organised in a busy environment. You will be part of a supportive team where collaboration, great service and a positive attitude really matter. The way we deliver healthcare continues to change, so you will need to be forward-thinking, flexible and ready to embrace new ways of working. Both full-time and part-time opportunities are potentially available. We can potentially be flexible for the right person, so if the role sounds like a great fit, wed be happy to discuss the hours that could work for both you and the practice. If you're a people person who enjoys problem-solving, multitasking and making a difference, we would love to hear from you. Our Patient Services Team is often the first point of contact for our patients, so you'll play a really important role in making sure they feel welcomed, listened to and supported. Whether you're helping someone at reception, speaking to them on the phone or dealing with an online request, you will help patients find the right support and make their experience with the practice as smooth as possible. No two days are quite the same. You will be involved in a wide variety of tasks, including: Helping patients with enquiries face-to-face, over the phone and online Booking appointments and helping patients access the most appropriate service for their needs Processing home visit requests and communicating test results Supporting new patient registrations and online access requests Processing referrals and keeping patient information accurate and up to date Monitoring practice communications and online systems to make sure important messages and updates are actioned Supporting our Online Triage service, including processing Anima requests and booking appointments following clinician guidance Managing tasks and waiting lists to help keep patient care moving Taking payments and completing routine daily administration Following practice procedures around confidentiality, safeguarding, health and safety and emergency situations You will work closely with patients, clinicians and colleagues across the practice, so great communication and teamwork are really important. As a member of our Patient Services Team, you will be at the heart of the patient experience. You will work closely with patients, clinicians and colleagues to make sure enquiries are handled professionally, information is accurate and patients are supported to access the right care. Patient Support & Communication Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and approachable manner, ensuring all enquiries are handled efficiently and confidentially. Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally, introducing yourself by name and taking appropriate action to support the caller. Listen to patient needs and signpost them to the most appropriate service, seeking advice from colleagues or clinicians where needed. Accurately book appointments, take messages and process home visit requests using the appropriate practice systems. Relay test results to patients in line with practice procedures. Deal sensitively and professionally with both positive and negative patient feedback, helping to resolve concerns where possible and involving the Patient Services Lead or Practice Manager when appropriate. Ensure important information and outstanding actions are clearly handed over to colleagues at shift changes. Online Triage & Patient Requests Regularly monitor Anima throughout the working day, ensuring requests are processed accurately and promptly. Process administrative requests received through Anima and respond to patients as appropriate. Action requests from GPs and NPs, including arranging appointments and following instructions or clinical comments. Support patients who contact us by telephone or face-to-face by creating an online triage request on their behalf where appropriate. Monitor task lists and waiting lists, contacting patients and booking appointments as required. Maintain accurate notes and update waiting lists where necessary. Monitor safeguarding DNA lists and follow the correct practice procedures for children and young people who do not attend appointments. Patient Administration Process new patient registrations, including both paper and online registrations through HealthTech. Process patient requests for online access and consent documentation through the appropriate practice and NHS systems. Ensure patient forms and documentation are recorded, distributed and processed accurately and promptly. Generate referrals to District Nursing and other services as required. Prepare sample pots and accompanying documentation for patient collection. Follow practice procedures regarding sample collection and patient information. Keeping Everything Running Smoothly Regularly check your individual and generic NHS email accounts, responding to and actioning messages promptly. Monitor TeamNet Clarity for practice updates, notifications, policy changes and outstanding or new training requirements. Ensure visitors are signed in correctly through TeamNet Clarity and provided with a visitor badge. Distribute documents, correspondence and incoming mail accurately and efficiently. Keep the patient waiting and reception areas welcoming, tidy, safe and appropriately staffed. Check and process NHS 111/CCAS requests throughout the working day. Attend and contribute to team, staff and other relevant meetings. Payments & Daily Administration Take patient payments and ensure transactions are recorded and processed accurately. Complete daily card machine reconciliation and banking processes. Complete routine administrative checks and end-of-day tasks to help ensure the smooth running of the practice. Safety & Practice Procedures Understand and follow practice confidentiality, safeguarding, health and safety procedures at all times. Be familiar with the practice panic alarm system and know how to respond appropriately when required. Understand and follow the practice fire evacuation procedure. Complete required fire alarm checks and ensure relevant evacuation lists can be produced when needed. Help maintain a safe, secure and welcoming environment for patients, visitors and colleagues.
